_about: Edits applied to src/aem-main.html by scripts/build-ncv-guide-review.py. IDs match ncv-guide-aem-review-2026-09-21.md. `find` is matched ignoring whitespace differences between tags and inside text; `occurrence` picks the nth match when the text appears more than once; `count` is the number of matches expected (default 1) and the build fails if it differs. Order matters: I-1 runs before P-9.

edits.title: First person: your role is the requirement; Concordia recommends 'I' (F-1)
edits.find: Yes — and it is not just permitted, it is the point. Funders want to understand your individual contribution to collaborative work. Using "we" throughout makes it impossible for reviewers to assess your specific role.
edits.replace: <!--rv:P-28-->Yes. The Tri-agency instructions ask you to explain your role in each contribution and leave the grammatical person open. Concordia recommends the first person because it states your role most directly. If every sentence says "we," reviewers cannot tell what you did.

edits.title: The change is rhetorical: make your own role visible (F-9)
edits.find: The biggest shift is not structural — it is rhetorical. A Narrative CV asks you to move from listing to explaining, and from passive to active voice.
edits.replace: <!--rv:P-29-->The main change is rhetorical. A narrative CV asks you to explain your contributions as well as list them, and to make your own role visible in each one.
